definition.name: Cut the Loss — the world's tactical calculation
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: When Morpheus is captured, the objective situation prices self-preservation as the only survivable move. Smith escalates to a doubled serum dosage that drives Morpheus's mind toward breaking, rendering him, in world-logic, a lost asset (ev-031, sc-144); the crew's own survival protocol is to pull Morpheus's plug rather than mount a rescue (ev-032, sc-148); and when the ship is hunted, Morpheus immediately converts to survival protocol — reading the Sentinels and ordering the EMP charged — the world's instinct being to preserve the ship, not gamble on one man (ev-040, sc-185). The world-level collision thus argues that the rational answer is to abandon the lost key and escape.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the world's first premise of loss: Smith's doubled serum drives Morpheus's mind toward breaking, which the world-logic prices as a lost asset — the key is no longer worth the risk, so the rational move becomes to cut him loose rather than gamble on him.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: The capture and the doubled dosage establish the material fact the world's arithmetic runs on — a breaking mind is a spent asset — which licenses every subsequent 'cut the loss' decision.

chain.why_in_plot: With the ship now hunted, the world's instinct surfaces unmediated: Morpheus reads the Sentinels, gives the crew minutes, and orders the EMP charged — preserving the ship, not gambling on any one man. This is the survival protocol in its pure form.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: The lost-asset valuation from the doubled serum (ev-031) clears the field of the 'save the man' option, so when the Sentinels arrive the crew's response is automatically the survivable move — charge the EMP and get out — with no rescue to weigh against it.

chain.why_in_plot: The Sentinels physically slam down on the Nebuchadnezzar while Morpheus drives the escape — the tactical calculation made flesh: the ship, not the man, is what must be preserved, and the rational move is to trigger the EMP.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-040: Morpheus's order to charge the EMP (ev-040) sets the ship on the escape trajectory; the Sentinel strike is that ordered move arriving at its execution point — the world closing the gap between the survival decision and the physical act of cutting loose.

chain.why_in_plot: As the Sentinels breach the hull, the crew gives Neo up — the monitors flatline and the rational answer is to accept the loss and escape. This is the cut-the-loss calculus at its peak: the world prices another life as a loss to be absorbed.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-042: The Sentinel ambush (ev-042) puts the ship in immediate mortal danger, so when Neo flatlines the crew's only survivable move is to accept him as a loss and get out — the physical pressure of the Sentinels makes 'give him up and flee' the world's verdict rather than a moment for grief.

chain.why_in_plot: The Sentinels overrun the deck and the crew's entire focus collapses into the single survivable move — getting out — the world's tactical calculation driving the final escape timing.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-044: Having already priced Neo as a loss to be accepted (ev-044), the world's arithmetic leaves only one rational action when the Sentinels overrun the deck: abandon the dead and trigger the escape — the flatline decision now executed as physical flight.

definition.name: The Wager on a Man — Neo's refusal of the arithmetic
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Neo resolves the dilemma from the inside by refusing its arithmetic. He explicitly denies he is the One, so going back carries no prophetic cover — only a pure wager on a man (ev-032, sc-148) — and because Morpheus already gave his life for him (ev-025, sc-115), self-preservation would cost his emerging self-respect a price he will not pay. That refusal to flee holds through to the end: cornered in the subway and urged to run, he turns back from the escalator to face the hunter (ev-038, sc-179).

chain.why_in_plot: Setup of the refusal-to-flee stance: Morpheus chooses to give his own life so the others can escape, laying down the debt of self-respect Neo will later refuse to cheapen by running.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Establishes the sacrifice that the rest of the arc is a response to — Neo's later refusal to flee is only a refusal because something was already paid for him.

chain.why_in_plot: Turn that raises the world's verdict: Morpheus is driven to the brink of breaking under a doubled serum, so Neo's choice to go back is made against the calculation that the asset is already lost.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: The life Morpheus gave in ev-025 is now being extracted from him in custody — his capture and the doubled serum are the cost of that sacrifice coming due, forcing the dilemma into the open.

chain.why_in_plot: The core turn of the arc: Neo stops the plug from being pulled and commits to going back, explicitly denying he is the One so the mission is a pure wager on a man rather than a prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: The world's verdict that Morpheus is about to break (ev-031) is exactly the arithmetic Neo refuses — he halts the unplug and goes back not as the One but as a man betting on a man.

chain.why_in_plot: The refusal-to-flee stance holds past the rescue: cornered in the subway and urged to run, Neo turns back from the escalator to face the hunter, hardening into a gunfighter's calm.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: The commitment to go back (ev-032) is tested again in a fresh flight-or-fight moment — the same refusal of the arithmetic now plays out as physical stillness when escape is offered.

chain.why_in_plot: Resolution: the wager's cost is paid in full — Neo dies having gone back for Morpheus — and the monitors jumping back to life resolve the self-preservation/self-sacrifice dilemma from the inside by refusing the arithmetic of loss.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-038: The stillness that refused flight (ev-038) leads Neo to stand and fight to the end, so he is shot and dies for the rescue — and the kiss that restores the monitors completes the refusal of the arithmetic the whole arc has been building.

definition.name: The Living Argument for Sacrifice — Morpheus's faith
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus is the embodied case for the sacrifice horn. He has already enacted it, giving his life so Neo and Trinity escape (ev-025, sc-115), and even while captured and drugged he spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than saving himself by betraying the crew (ev-031, sc-144). After the rescue, his faith reframes Neo's illogical gamble as destiny, reinterpreting the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One (ev-035, sc-170), pressing the belief that a man is worth any risk.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the sacrifice horn enacted rather than merely argued: when an Agent ambushes Neo in the crawlspace, Morpheus pins it down and orders Trinity to get Neo out, choosing to give his own life so the others escape. definition.name: Loyalty Over Survival — the Neo–Trinity bond
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: The Neo–Trinity bond is where the dilemma is felt as loyalty versus survival. Gutted by Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, Trinity converts grief into command and makes the rescue possible only on her terms, binding herself to Neo's wager (ev-032, sc-148); the bond's protective reciprocity runs even amid escape, when Neo breaks free of her embrace and sends her out first (ev-030, sc-142); and their 'we' ultimately overrides the world's cut-the-loss verdict, as Trinity refuses to accept Neo's death — kissing him until the monitors jump back to life (ev-044, sc-209).

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus's sacrifice is the debt the Neo–Trinity bond spends the rest of the arc answering: he gives his life so the two of them escape, and specifically orders Trinity to get Neo out — so from the start the bond is built on one of them being handed over to the other's keeping. definition.name: A Community Wrestling the Question — the crew's split
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: The crew collectively lives out both horns. Cypher embodies self-preservation to its logical end — first recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a mere 'body count' to retreat Neo toward caution (ev-020, sc-073), then murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, only to be struck down by the surviving Tank (ev-029, sc-137). The rest of the crew — Tank, Switch, Apoc, Dozer — pay the price of the sacrifice horn, and their split between doubters and believers during Neo's failed jump shows a community wrestling with whether any one man is worth dying for (ev-016, sc-058).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the community's first open fracture over the dilemma: as Neo runs the rooftop jump, the crew on the main deck splits into doubters and believers, and the failed attempt forces the whole group to wrestle with whether any single man is worth dying for — the question the rest of the plot spends
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: The shared training session is the plot's ground zero; it places the entire crew in one room watching one man risk himself, which is exactly what lets the group divide into doubters and believers instead of individuals deciding in private.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher voices the self-preservation horn to the community, recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a mere 'body count' to pull Neo toward caution, and then, in the Matrix, seals the betrayal that will cost the crew their lives — the retreat-horn spoken aloud inside the group
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: The failed jump leaves the crew's faith exposed and contestable (Neo fell, the group split), and Cypher answers that exposed question by reframing Morpheus's belief as a lethal 'body count' — turning the group's silent 'is he worth it?' into an argument for caution and self-preservation.

chain.why_in_plot: Self-preservation reaches its logical end inside the community: Cypher murders Apoc and Switch and delivers Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, and the surviving Tank strikes him down — the crew literally killing and being killed by its own split
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-020: The steak-restaurant bargain with Agent Smith (sc-074, ev-020) is the contract that Cypher executes aboard the ship here: the treachery he sealed in the Matrix becomes open murder and the handover of Morpheus, so the deal struck in ev-020 is the direct cause of the deaths and capture in ev-029.
